claims.claim: 7. How TimeLog rows sync (tombstoned, delete-wins, last-writer-wins).

evidence.quote: local.deletedAt == null && entity.deletedAt != null -> timeLogDao.softDelete(local.id, entity.deletedAt)

missed.fact: The map omitted four columns: id (Long autoincrement PK, local only, not synced), uid (String NOT NULL, unique index, the cross-device identity), deletedAt (Instant? soft-delete tombstone) and updatedAt (Instant NOT NULL, bumped on every write). Sync keys on uid, and the owner travels as entryUid/habitUid, never as the local Long id.

The exactly-one-owner rule is not a DB constraint. It is enforced only by the TrackTarget sealed interface, and TimeLog.target() throws on an ownerless row. A sync record with neither owner uid resolved is held back and not inserted, so a free-standing interval cannot merge in.

Two ordinary soft-delete paths exist for entries and habits (EntryDao.softDelete, HabitDao.softDelete). They only set deletedAt on the parent and do not touch time_logs. The CASCADE fires only on the hard deleteForever/deleteAll path, so a time log survives a soft-deleted parent and is still counted. Whether the UI path goes through soft or hard delete was not traced.

TimeLogDao.softDelete exists and sync calls it, but the only timeTracker calls in shared/src are start, stop, toggle, running, logsOn and logsForHabit. No UI path deletes or edits a log, so tombstones originate only from a remote device's snapshot.

loggedMinutes sums each log's clipped duration independently, so overlapping logs are counted twice. Overlap is unlikely locally because start() closes any open log, but after a merge two devices' open logs can both run until the next start or stop, and then overlap.

Day totals select logs by start time, not by overlap. A log that crosses midnight counts wholly to its start day in the DAO query (observeBetween), but loggedSpans clips it at 24:00. Week summaries use loggedMinutes clipped to the window, so the two rules differ.
The per-entry and per-habit totals on the Tasks/Habits list come from loggedByEntry/loggedByHabit over only today's logs (logsOn(LocalDate.now())), not all-time.
A stale remote update to a locally tombstoned log is ignored (delete wins). When both sides are live, the later updatedAt wins, which is how an open log and its later close merge.
